current_evidence: The council's 'Apply for planning permission' page points to this web page ('See the planning application validation requirements page for full details'), and a site search found no separate or newer local list PDF; the page carries no adoption or update date, so Grokbot's 'Undated' is correct.

issues.detail: Householder is shown as '(none) - national requirements only', but the page has a householder section with local requirements: block plan (1:100/1:200), floor plans, elevations, roof plans and sections/levels; Flood Risk Assessment (flood zones 2/3/3b, zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more, critical drainage areas); bat scoping survey (in or near a bat alert zone or known roost); TPO tree plan showing species and protection measures (where a TPO is on site); photographs of all elevations (retrospective applications); position photos and manufacturer's specification (satellite dishes); and a noise impact assessment (plant or machinery such as wind turbines, pools or air conditioning).

Grokbot has only 13 requirement rows against roughly 40 local items on the page. These have no app_type row at all, or appear only as broken fragments in tab_items: Coal recovery report (coal recovery areas; not needed in a High Risk Area); Daylight/sunlight assessment (adverse impact on current light levels); Environmental and amenity impact report (energy, waste and minerals development); Glint and glare assessment (development that could cause solar reflection); Land contamination (vulnerable uses need a Phase 1; single houses in gardens need a historic map review from 1850; low-vulnerability uses on brownfield land or within 250m of a landfill); Landscaping (all applications, plus a 1:200 plan for majors); Lighting assessment (external lighting in residential or conservation areas); Parking provision; Planning obligations draft heads of terms; Sand and gravel safeguarding (over 1 ha in a safeguarding area) and a minerals/waste safeguarding justification statement; Statement of Community Involvement (major and sensitive schemes); Sustainability statement (all majors, plus BREEAM for non-residential majors); Tall buildings design statement and Wind study (buildings substantially taller than neighbours); Town centre sequential test (main town centre uses outside a centre; extensions of 200 sq m or less exempt); Town centre impact assessment (retail/leisure over 2,500 sq m outside a centre); Transport assessment/statement and Travel plan (significant transport implications, using the Leeds Transport SPD thresholds); Ventilation/extraction (restaurants, cafes, pubs, takeaways, and large uses with substantial extraction); Visual representations (majors and proposals affecting conservation areas); Waste and refuse storage (all developments); Wind turbines and birds (non-EIA turbines within 1 km of the South Pennine Moors SPA); Onshore wind (more than 2 turbines or hub height over 15m, with compulsory community pre-application consultation).
issues.evidence: Validation requirements page, 'Planning applications' local list headings.

issues.detail: Every Full planning row is tagged 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', even where the page names the application type. Examples: 'Lawful development evidence (sworn affidavit or tenancy agreements)' is placed under Full planning, but it belongs to Certificates of Existing Use, which Grokbot shows as '(none)'. The noise 'plant/machinery' trigger and the bat scoping survey come from the householder section. Outline and Reserved matters are shown as '(none)', yet the Coal Mining Risk Assessment applies to 'full and outline non-householder' applications and the minerals safeguarding justification statement applies to full, outline and reserved matters applications.
issues.evidence: Page sections 'Certificates of Existing or Proposed Use' and 'Coal Mining Risk Assessment: full and outline non-householder applications in Development High Risk Areas'.

issues.detail: Several application types are shown as '(none)' although the page sets local requirements for them. Advertisement consent: 1:50/1:100 drawings with size, siting, materials, colours, projection, illumination method and cross-section; external lighting details (hours of use, light pollution, shrouds); photographs or photomontages. Prior notifications: demolition needs a bat survey where relevant, photographs, tree survey, 1:200 landscaping plan and possibly a structural survey; telecoms needs evidence of notice to owners, notice for masts within 3 km of an aerodrome and an acoustic report. Works to trees: local additions are photographs and evidence of advice sought, and s211 notices need a detailed tree plan with street names and house numbers. Discharge of conditions: the relevant drawings and the permission and condition numbers.
issues.evidence: Page sections 'Advertisement applications', 'Prior notifications', 'Tree works' and 'Approval (discharge) of conditions'.

issues.detail: Listed building consent captures only the schedule of works and structural survey. It misses these listed-building requirements: detail drawings at 1:20 for features being altered, with manufacturer specifications; interior, exterior and setting photographs with a location plan; a condition survey (where historic fabric is replaced); a conservation area impact assessment (sites within or adjacent to a conservation area); and a tree survey and protected species report where relevant.

The Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment trigger quotes the coal recovery exemption ('If the site is also within a High Risk Area ... a separate report is not required') rather than the actual trigger. The real trigger is full and outline non-householder applications in a Coal Authority Development High Risk Area involving ground disturbance, with sheds, fences, walls, street furniture and shop fronts exempt.
issues.evidence: Page: 'Coal Mining Risk Assessment: full and outline non-householder applications in Development High Risk Areas'.

issues.detail: Several trigger excerpts are cut-off fragments or come from the wrong item. Design and Access Statement quotes photograph guidance ('These can form part of the design and access statement...'). Environmental Statement quotes boilerplate about plans and block plans; the real trigger is Schedule 1 development, or Schedule 2 where screening finds significant effects. Drainage Strategy quotes 'then only a drainage plan showing pipe sizes...'; the real triggers are sites of 1 ha or more in zone 1 and new development in zones 2/3, a Surface Water Drainage Assessment above the 250 m2 minor threshold, and a Conceptual SuDS Design Assessment for majors. Flood Risk Assessment starts mid-sentence ('size, then a Flood Risk Assessment...'); the real trigger is flood zones 2/3, zone 1 sites of 1 ha or more, and critical drainage areas. Heritage statement gives no trigger; it applies to proposals affecting a heritage asset or its setting, demolition in conservation areas and LBC applications.
issues.evidence: Flood Risk and Surface Water Drainage validation PDF (FRA triggers listed) and the validation requirements page.

issues.detail: The Noise Impact Assessment under Full planning uses the householder plant/machinery wording only. The full-application trigger covers noise-sensitive uses, listed use classes (E(c), E(d), sui generis pubs and takeaways, F2), industry in town centres, and development near noise sources or residential uses.
issues.evidence: Page 'Noise assessment' entry under Planning applications.

issues.detail: Most tab_items are link text, reference lists or contact details rather than requirements. Examples: 'Bat alert zones in the Leeds district (PDF, 8.3MB)'; 'References Leeds Transport SPD (PDF, 12.7MB) ...'; 'References Tall Buildings Design Guide ...'; 'References Guidance on Transport Assessment (PDF, 364KB) GOV.UK Guidance:'; 'The Flood Risk requirements table (PDF, 77KB) outlines...'; and the FRM email contact 'e mail FRM@leeds.gov.uk ... respond within five working days'. Several items also merge two or three different requirements into one run-on string (air quality, travel plan, town centre).

The 'Existing and proposed site levels / sections' trigger is taken from the flood PDF ('if raised Finished Floor Levels...'). On the validation page, sections and levels at 1:50/1:100 are a standard required drawing for householder and full applications.
issues.evidence: Page 'Local requirements - plans and drawings' for householder and full applications.

summary: Grokbot's link is the current Leeds local list. The list is an undated web page, with a supporting flood risk and drainage PDF. The extraction is badly incomplete: it captures about 13 of roughly 40 local requirements, shows Householder, Advertisement, Lawful development, Prior approval and Tree works as '(none)' although the page sets local requirements for each, and several triggers are fragments or come from the wrong item.
